To give back to this wonderful sub, I would like to create a how-to for meditation. There are a lot of people who have read up on meditation and think "wow, there sure are a lot of benefits. Maybe I should try this." So then you sit down like a hindu and try really hard to meditate. You don't really know what you're doing, what you're trying to accomplish, or how much time has passed. You mind is not quieted, you focused too hard on the effects you think you should receive and you stand up feeling quasi-relaxed, but half frustrated. You may think you can't do it, but you can.

Just a few months ago I began meditating every day and promised myself that I will meditate every day of 2017. I have not missed a single day. So without further ado, let's get into it.

Sit Down - Naturally, you may not want to stand during this exercise (and it is an exercise). Contrary to pop-culture references, you don't need to cross your legs when you meditate and sit on the floor. You can, but you don't need to. When you start, you need to have minimal distractions and that includes body discomfort. So sit in a chair, or on the couch. Just make sure you are comfortable. Rest your hands gently in your lap and place your feet flat on the ground (if you can). Laying down in not recommended as it is easier to fall asleep. I have only fallen asleep once this way, but in my defense I was very sick.

Warm-up - So now you're on the runway, but you're not ready to take off yet. Close your eyes and scan your body. Are you relaxed? How are your shoulders? Your hands? Your belly, back, legs? Are they rigid and firm or relaxed and soft? How is your brow? Is it scrunched up or relaxed? Is your jaw tight and closed or loose and open? Make sure to relax your body as best you can.

Mediation - Oh boy, here we go! Ideally you want to quit your mind. Think no thoughts. If it was simply that easy, everyone would do it. It's difficult. Our brain wants to wander. Instead give your monkey-mind something to do. Concentrate on your breath. A great technique is the 4-fold breath. Breath counting to 4. Hold for 4. Breath out counting to 4. Your mind will wander to all the little things in your life. Observe those thoughts, but don't get lost in them. If you feel you are getting distracted, come back to your breath. This is really it. It sounds very simple, but you will find in practice that it isn't. And that's fine.

Practice non-judgement - You will want to get frustrated. You might not go as long as you want, or your mind wandered too much, or you were distracted by a pain. So what? It's not a problem unless you label it a problem. Simply try again next time. Mediation is an exercise for thought and emotion. You must learn to not be a victim of your emotions, they are at your mercy. You are the master of your fate, you are the captain of your soul.

Practice daily - This is the key. Consistency. Mediation once a week will not do you any favors. You must do it daily and ideally around the same time of day (best for habit formation). Set a reminder if you need to. Do this every day for a month and analyze how it has affected you. Those around you may notice a difference before you do.

Time - There is no required time to get a benefit, but I have personally noticed a greater profit from longer times. I would begin with 5 minutes. Once you can reliably go 5 minutes, go 6. Then 7, 8, 9, ad infinitum. It really is a beautiful thing. You can either set a timer, or simply peek at a clock for your time. I do a little of both.

That's really it. As far as resources, I highly recommend "Insight Timer" from the playstore. It's free, has guided meditations (good for beginners, but don't rely on them too much), has very soft bells for their timers, and a wide array of guided categories (spoken, chakras, binaural beats, nature sounds, music, chanting, etc).

I didn't want to get too crazy with this guide, because I want you to get meditating right away! Go, right now. What are you doing that you can't sacrifice 5 minutes?

Please let me know if you have any questions. Namaste.
